circuit:Abu Dhabi.title: Yas Marina Circuit
circuit:Abu Dhabi.summary: Yas Marina Circuit on Yas Island in Abu Dhabi is a 5. 281 km track designed by Hermann Tilke that has served as the venue for Formula One's season-closing Abu Dhabi Grand Prix since 2009. The circuit represents the second of four Middle Eastern Formula One venues, following Bahrain's establishment and preceding those in Qatar and Saudi Arabia.

circuit:Australia.title: Albert Park Circuit
circuit:Australia.summary: The Albert Park Circuit is a street course that encircles Albert Park Lake in Melbourne's Albert Park suburb and holds FIA Grade 1 status. It serves as the permanent home for the Formula One Australian Grand Prix, alongside various supporting racing series held throughout the year.

circuit:Austria.title: Red Bull Ring
circuit:Austria.summary: Located in Spielberg, Austria, this 4. 326 km circuit served as the Austrian Grand Prix venue across two separate periods: initially as Österreichring from 1970 to 1987, then after being shortened and reconstructed as the A1-Ring from 1997 to 2003. The facility has since been further modified and rebranded to reflect its current sponsorship arrangements.

circuit:Azerbaijan.title: Baku City Circuit
circuit:Azerbaijan.summary: The Baku City Circuit is a street circuit in Azerbaijan's capital city situated along Baku Boulevard, spanning 6. 003 km per lap to rank as the fourth-longest venue in Formula One. The track hosted its inaugural F1 race as the 2016 European Grand Prix, before becoming home to the Azerbaijan Grand Prix starting in 2017.

circuit:Bahrain.title: Bahrain International Circuit
circuit:Bahrain.summary: Opened in 2004, the Bahrain International Circuit is a 5. 412 km venue that hosted the inaugural Formula One race held in the Middle East that same year. The track accommodates various motorsport events including the annual Bahrain Grand Prix, GP2 Series, drag racing, and 24-hour endurance competitions, operating under FIA Grade 1 certification with multiple configurable layouts.

circuit:Barcelona.title: Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya
circuit:Barcelona.summary: Located in Montmeló near Barcelona, this 4. 657 km Spanish circuit features a balanced blend of extended straights and diverse corner configurations that test multiple aspects of driver skill and car performance. The venue holds FIA Grade 1 status and accommodates approximately 140,700 spectators across its grandstands.

circuit:Belgium.title: Circuit de Spa-Francorchamps
circuit:Belgium.summary: This Belgian circuit, stretching 7. 004 kilometers through the Ardennes region near Stavelot, has been a cornerstone of Formula One racing since the sport's inaugural 1950 season. The venue has continuously hosted the Belgian Grand Prix since 1985, with only two absences in 2003 and 2006, establishing itself as one of the championship's most enduring and prestigious racing destinations.

circuit:Canada.title: Circuit Gilles Villeneuve
circuit:Canada.summary: Located on Notre Dame Island in Montreal, Quebec, this 4. 361-kilometer temporary circuit serves as the home of Canada's Formula One Grand Prix. Beyond Formula One, the track has accommodated various international racing series including sports car championships and North American open-wheel and stock car competitions.

circuit:China.title: Shanghai International Circuit
circuit:China.summary: The Shanghai International Circuit, located in Shanghai's Jiading district, is a motorsport venue renowned for hosting the Chinese Grand Prix, which ran annually from 2004 to 2019 before resuming in 2024. The track has also begun accommodating electric racing events starting in 2024.

circuit:Great Britain.title: Silverstone Circuit
circuit:Great Britain.summary: Silverstone, located in the English Midlands near Northamptonshire, established itself as the venue for Britain's premier motorsport event when it inaugural hosted the national Grand Prix in 1948. The circuit gained further historical significance by staging the opening round of the inaugural Formula One World Championship in 1950, though the British Grand Prix subsequently alternated between three venues until returning permanently to Silverstone from 1987 onward. Beyond Formula One, the track also serves as host to the British round of the motorcycle racing world championship.

circuit:Hungary.title: Hungaroring
circuit:Hungary.summary: The Hungaroring, a 4. 381 km permanent circuit located near Budapest in Hungary, hosted the sport's first Grand Prix within the Eastern Bloc when it opened in 1986. Built in just eight months, faster than any other Formula One track, the venue was constructed outside the city following government preference over initial plans for a street course through Budapest's central park.

circuit:Italy.title: Autodromo Nazionale Monza
circuit:Italy.summary: Situated near Milan in northern Italy, the Monza circuit is a 5. 793 km track constructed in 1922 as mainland Europe's earliest purpose-built racing facility. Home to the Italian Grand Prix since 1949, with only a brief absence in 1980, it stands among the select few venues that have remained fixtures on the Formula One calendar from the sport's inception, earning the nickname "Temple of Speed" for its notably long straightaways and fast-flowing corners.

circuit:Japan.title: Suzuka International Racing Course
circuit:Japan.summary: Suzuka Circuit, located in Mie Prefecture, Japan, spans 5. 807 kilometers and serves as a premier venue for Formula One and Super Formula racing. The track, operated by Honda's subsidiary, accommodates 155,000 spectators and remains one of motorsport's most prestigious racing destinations.

circuit:Las Vegas.title: Las Vegas Strip Circuit
circuit:Las Vegas.summary: The Las Vegas Strip Circuit is a street track that winds through Paradise, Nevada, incorporating the famous Las Vegas Boulevard and its iconic hotels and casinos. The layout navigates past prominent venues such as MSG Sphere, Caesars Palace, Bellagio, and Paris Las Vegas, creating a unique urban racing environment in one of the world's most recognizable entertainment destinations.

circuit:Mexico City.title: Autódromo Hermanos Rodríguez
circuit:Mexico City.summary: Located in Mexico City, the 4. 304 km Autódromo Hermanos Rodríguez is named in tribute to brothers Ricardo and Pedro Rodríguez, both of whom died in racing accidents. The circuit has hosted Formula One's Mexican Grand Prix during three distinct eras, most recently from 2015 onwards under its current "Mexico City Grand Prix" designation, following earlier hosting periods that ended in 1992.

circuit:Miami.title: Miami International Autodrome
circuit:Miami.summary: The Miami International Autodrome is a temporary track constructed around Hard Rock Stadium in Miami Gardens, featuring a 3. 363-mile layout with 19 corners that generates average qualifying speeds near 139 mph. Created by specialist racing circuit designers for the Miami Grand Prix's debut on the Formula One calendar in 2022, the venue has since expanded its motorsport profile to include Formula E racing from the 2025–26 season using an adapted configuration.

circuit:Monaco.title: Circuit de Monaco
circuit:Monaco.summary: The Circuit de Monaco is a 3. 337 km street course that winds through the Monte Carlo and La Condamine districts of Monaco, incorporating the harbour area into its layout. Though technically spanning multiple neighbourhoods, it is widely known as the Monte Carlo circuit due to its predominant location within that district.

circuit:Netherlands.title: Circuit Zandvoort
circuit:Netherlands.summary: Located in the Dutch coastal dunes northwest of Amsterdam, the 4. 259 km Zandvoort circuit hosted the Dutch Grand Prix after its return to the Formula One calendar in 2021. The partnership between the track and Formula One concluded at the end of 2026.

circuit:Qatar.title: Lusail International Circuit
circuit:Qatar.summary: Situated north of Doha in Qatar, the Lusail International Circuit is a 5. 419 km track featuring a 1. 068 km main straight and holds FIA Grade 1 certification.

circuit:São Paulo.title: Autódromo José Carlos Pace
circuit:São Paulo.summary: Interlagos is a 4. 309 km Brazilian racing facility in São Paulo that opened in 1940 and was later dedicated to the memory of Formula 1 driver José Carlos Pace following his 1977 death. The counterclockwise track has hosted numerous grands prix and features additional amenities including a karting venue named after fellow Brazilian racing legend Ayrton Senna.

circuit:Saudi Arabia.title: Jeddah Corniche Circuit
circuit:Saudi Arabia.summary: The Jeddah Corniche Circuit is a street racing venue situated along Saudi Arabia's Red Sea waterfront that has been home to the Formula One Saudi Arabian Grand Prix since its inaugural 2021 running. The facility also began hosting the Formula E championship event in 2025.

circuit:Singapore.title: Marina Bay Street Circuit
circuit:Singapore.summary: The Marina Bay Street Circuit winds through Singapore's Marina Bay area, incorporating the Downtown Core and Kallang districts within its layout.

circuit:Spain.title: Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya
circuit:Spain.summary: The Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya, located near Barcelona in Catalonia, stretches 4. 657 kilometers and features a balanced mix of lengthy straightaways and diverse corner configurations, making it a versatile test for racing machinery. The venue holds FIA Grade 1 certification and accommodates approximately 140,700 spectators across its stands.

circuit:United States.title: Circuit of the Americas
circuit:United States.summary: Located in Austin, Texas, the Circuit of the Americas is a 3. 426-mile FIA Grade 1 facility that serves as the permanent home of the United States Grand Prix in Formula One. Beyond single-seater racing, the venue hosts multiple motorsport categories including MotoGP's Motorcycle Grand Prix of the Americas and the Lone Star Le Mans endurance event, alongside having previously accommodated various other racing series.

driver:ALB.title: Alexander Albon
driver:ALB.summary: Alexander Albon is a dual Thai and British motorsport competitor who currently races for Williams in Formula One, representing Thailand internationally.

driver:ALO.title: Fernando Alonso
driver:ALO.summary: Spanish driver Fernando Alonso, currently racing for Aston Martin, has secured two Formula One world titles during his 23-season career with Renault, along with 32 Grand Prix victories. Beyond single-seaters, Alonso has demonstrated versatility in endurance racing, claiming the 2018-19 World Endurance Championship and two Le Mans victories with Toyota, making him the sole driver to win both the Formula One and World Endurance championships.

driver:ANT.title: Andrea Kimi Antonelli
driver:ANT.summary: Italian driver Andrea Kimi Antonelli races for Mercedes in Formula One, having accumulated eight Grand Prix victories since entering the sport in 2025.

driver:BEA.title: Oliver Bearman
driver:BEA.summary: British racing driver Oliver Bearman currently races for Haas in Formula One, competing at the highest level of motorsport.

driver:BOR.title: Gabriel Bortoleto
driver:BOR.summary: Brazilian driver Gabi Bortoleto currently races in Formula One for Audi, competing at the highest level of motorsport.

driver:BOT.title: Valtteri Bottas
driver:BOT.summary: Finnish driver Valtteri Bottas currently races for Cadillac in Formula One after a lengthy career spanning 13 seasons. He achieved two runner-up finishes in the drivers' championship while competing for Mercedes, and has claimed victory in 10 Grand Prix events throughout his time in the sport.

driver:COL.title: Franco Colapinto
driver:COL.summary: Franco Alejandro Colapinto is an Argentine driver competing in Formula One, currently representing Alpine on the grid.

driver:DOO.title: Jack Doohan (racing driver)
driver:DOO.summary: Jack Doohan, an Australian racer, holds a reserve driver position with Haas while competing in European Le Mans Series prototype racing. He has made limited Formula One appearances, taking part in seven Grand Prix events during the 2024-2025 season.

driver:GAS.title: Pierre Gasly
driver:GAS.summary: Pierre Gasly is a French Formula One driver currently racing for Alpine. The driver achieved his sole Grand Prix victory at the 2020 Italian Grand Prix during his time with AlphaTauri.

driver:HAD.title: Isack Hadjar
driver:HAD.summary: Isack Alexandre Hadjar, a driver holding both French and Algerian nationality, currently races for Red Bull Racing in Formula One under the French banner.

driver:HAM.title: Lewis Hamilton
driver:HAM.summary: Lewis Hamilton is a British Formula One driver currently racing for Ferrari, holding an equal-record seven world championship titles alongside Michael Schumacher. He leads the sport in multiple categories including race victories, pole positions, and podium appearances.

driver:HUL.title: Nico Hülkenberg
driver:HUL.summary: German driver Nicolas Hülkenberg currently races for Audi in Formula One. Beyond his single-seater career, he achieved significant success in sports car racing, notably winning the prestigious 24 Hours of Le Mans in 2015 while driving for Porsche.

driver:LAW.title: Liam Lawson
driver:LAW.summary: Liam Lawson is a New Zealand-born racing driver currently competing in Formula One with the Racing Bulls team.

driver:LEC.title: Charles Leclerc
driver:LEC.summary: The Monaco-born driver races for Ferrari in Formula One, having achieved nine career race victories over nine seasons. He came closest to the world championship in 2022 when he finished as runner-up in the drivers' standings.

driver:MAG.title: Kevin Magnussen
driver:MAG.summary: Danish driver Kevin Magnussen, known as K-Mag, raced in Formula One across two separate periods, from 2014-2020 and again from 2022-2024. Following his F1 career, he transitioned to competing in the World Endurance Championship with BMW through WRT, while also contesting selected NASCAR Cup Series events for Trackhouse Racing.

driver:NOR.title: Lando Norris
driver:NOR.summary: Lando Norris is a British Formula One driver competing for McLaren, where he claimed the 2025 drivers' championship. Across his eight seasons in the sport, he has secured 13 Grand Prix victories.

driver:OCO.title: Esteban Ocon
driver:OCO.summary: Esteban Ocon is a French racing driver currently competing in Formula One with the Haas team.

driver:PER.title: Sergio Pérez
driver:PER.summary: Mexican driver Sergio Pérez competes for Cadillac in Formula One, bringing extensive experience from 15 seasons in the sport. He finished second in the 2023 championship standings while driving for Red Bull and has claimed six race victories throughout his career.

driver:PIA.title: Oscar Piastri
driver:PIA.summary: Oscar Piastri is an Australian driver competing for McLaren in Formula One, having secured nine Grand Prix victories throughout his four seasons in the sport.

driver:RIC.title: Daniel Ricciardo
driver:RIC.summary: Daniel Ricciardo, an Australian driver known by the moniker "the Honey Badger," competed in Formula One over a 14-year span from 2011 through 2024, securing eight Grand Prix victories during his career in the sport.

driver:RUS.title: George Russell (racing driver)
driver:RUS.summary: George Russell, a British driver, has claimed eight Grand Prix victories during his eight-year Formula One career with Mercedes.

driver:SAI.title: Carlos Sainz Jr.
driver:SAI.summary: Carlos Sainz Jr. is a Spanish driver competing in Formula One for Williams, bringing over a decade of experience to the grid. Throughout his 12-season career, he has secured four Grand Prix victories.

driver:SAR.title: Logan Sargeant
driver:SAR.summary: Logan Sargeant is an American driver who recently concluded his Formula One career after competing during 2023 and 2024. He now races in the FIA World Endurance Championship's LMGT3 category with Proton Competition, having previously driven LMP2 machinery for Era Motorsport in IMSA competition.

driver:STR.title: Lance Stroll
driver:STR.summary: Lance Stroll is a Canadian Formula One driver currently competing for Aston Martin in the sport's top championship series.

driver:TSU.title: Yuki Tsunoda
driver:TSU.summary: Japanese driver Yuki Tsunoda spent five seasons as a full-time Formula One competitor starting in 2021 before transitioning to a reserve role with Red Bull Racing and its sister team Racing Bulls in 2026.

driver:VER.title: Max Verstappen
driver:VER.summary: The Dutch-Belgian driver has established himself as one of Formula One's most successful competitors, capturing four consecutive world championships between 2021 and 2024 while representing Red Bull Racing. With 71 Grand Prix victories accumulated over 12 seasons, he continues to compete for the team under the Dutch flag.

driver:ZHO.title: Zhou Guanyu
driver:ZHO.summary: Zhou Guanyu is a Chinese racing driver and the sole representative from China to have participated in Formula One, competing in the sport between 2022 and 2024. He currently holds a reserve driver position with Cadillac in the championship.

team:Alpine.title: Alpine F1 Team
team:Alpine.summary: The Enstone-based team has operated under the Alpine Racing name since 2021, when Renault rebranded its works squad to highlight its Alpine sports car division. Following Renault's ownership period, the team competed as Renault's official entry until the automotive manufacturer's withdrawal from the championship at the conclusion of 2025.

team:Aston Martin.title: Aston Martin in Formula One
team:Aston Martin.summary: Aston Martin has competed in Formula One across multiple eras as a British manufacturer. The modern incarnation operates as AMR GP Limited and currently races under the Aston Martin Aramco branding.

team:Ferrari.title: Scuderia Ferrari
team:Ferrari.summary: Scuderia Ferrari represents the motorsport arm of the Italian luxury automaker Ferrari and stands as Formula One's longest-running and most accomplished outfit, participating continuously since the championship's inception in 1950. The team, famously nicknamed after its emblem, has maintained an unbroken presence throughout the sport's entire history.

team:Haas F1 Team.title: Haas F1 Team
team:Haas F1 Team.summary: Gene Haas founded this American-licensed Formula One team in 2014, with the outfit entering the sport for the first time in 2016. Leadership changed hands in early 2024 when Ayao Komatsu took over as team principal from Guenther Steiner, who had guided the squad since its establishment.

team:Kick Sauber.title: Sauber Motorsport
team:Kick Sauber.summary: Sauber, a Swiss engineering firm established in 1970, progressed from building sports cars to becoming an independent Formula One constructor starting in 1993. The outfit claimed two endurance racing world championships and won the 1989 Le Mans 24 Hours before departing Formula One in 2025 as the sport's fourth-longest-tenured constructor. Audi acquired the team and its operations in 2024 to establish the technical foundation for its own factory effort.

team:McLaren.title: McLaren
team:McLaren.summary: McLaren Racing is a British Formula One outfit headquartered in Woking that operates as a subsidiary of the McLaren Group under Mumtalakat Holding Company's ownership. The team competes in the sport from its base at the McLaren Technology Centre.

team:Mercedes.title: Mercedes-AMG Petronas F1 Team
team:Mercedes.summary: Mercedes has maintained a presence in Formula One since 1954 as both a constructor and engine supplier. The current iteration, competing as Mercedes-AMG Petronas Formula One Team from their Brackley base, gained Ineos as an equal partner alongside Mercedes-Benz Group and team principal Toto Wolff in 2022. The marque's racing teams are traditionally known by the "Silver Arrows" designation.

team:Racing Bulls.title: Racing Bulls
team:Racing Bulls.summary: Racing Bulls is an Italian Formula One constructor that joined the grid in 2024, operating as one of two teams owned by Red Bull GmbH alongside Red Bull Racing. Based in Faenza with an additional facility near its Milton Keynes sister team, the squad represents Red Bull's dual-team strategy in the championship.

team:RB.title: Racing Bulls
team:RB.summary: Racing Bulls is an Italian Formula One constructor that began competing in 2024 as part of Red Bull GmbH's portfolio alongside Red Bull Racing. Headquartered in Faenza with a secondary facility near Milton Keynes, the team operates as one of two constructors owned by the Austrian conglomerate.

team:Red Bull Racing.title: Red Bull Racing
team:Red Bull Racing.summary: Red Bull Racing, based in England under an Austrian licence, became a dominant Formula One force following its 2005 establishment as part of the Red Bull GmbH portfolio. Christian Horner led the team throughout its two-decade tenure before Laurent Mekies assumed management in 2025, with the outfit now operating alongside Red Bull's second F1 entry, Racing Bulls.

team:Williams.title: Williams Racing
team:Williams.summary: Williams Grand Prix Engineering, established in 1977 by Frank Williams and Patrick Head following the collapse of Williams's previous racing venture, is a British Formula One constructor headquartered in Grove, Oxfordshire. The team competes in the 2026 season as Atlassian Williams F1 Team and operates from a substantial purpose-built facility in the English countryside.
